profiles.note: Device-class buckets (role × vendor). Attach Metric sets here; nodes inherit them via their profile.
profiles.unavailable: Profile management is unavailable in skeleton mode (no metadata store).

empty.noneSub: Add a device-class profile (e.g. “Cisco Catalyst switch”).

modal.pollIntervalPlaceholder: leave blank to use the system default
modal.pollIntervalHint: Overrides the system default for nodes using this profile. 10–3600 seconds; leave blank to inherit the default.

delete.confirm: Delete profile {{name}}? Nodes using it keep running but lose this class's collection defaults.

templates.empty: No metric sets exist yet. Create some first.

err.pollInterval: Poll interval must be a whole number of seconds between 10 and 3600.

rules.note: Map a discovered device's sysObjectID / sysDescr to a Device profile. Discovery pre-selects the match on import.
rules.unavailable: Classification-rule management is unavailable in skeleton mode (no metadata store).

empty.noneSub: Add a rule mapping a sysObjectID prefix or sysDescr pattern to a profile.

modal.oidPrefixHint: Authoritative — outranks sysDescr. End with a dot so 1.3…9. won't also match …91. Pair with a sysDescr regex to split one vendor by NOS.
modal.descrRegexHintBoth: With a prefix set, both must match (vendor + NOS); on its own, it matches sysDescr directly.
modal.matcherRequired: Provide a sysObjectID prefix and/or a sysDescr regex.

delete.confirm: Delete the rule mapping {{sig}} → {{profile}}? Discovery will stop suggesting this profile for matching devices (already-imported nodes are unaffected).

sets.note: Reusable metric bundles. Attach them to device profiles; editing one updates every profile that uses it.
sets.unavailable: Metric sets are unavailable in skeleton mode (no metadata store).

empty.noneSub: Add a reusable metric bundle (e.g. “Standard interfaces”).

delete.confirm: Delete metric set {{name}}? Profiles that attach it lose this bundle's metrics.

editor.pickerSearchPlaceholder: Search the MIB catalog by name / OID / vendor…
editor.emptyTemplate: No metrics in this set yet.
editor.emptyNode: No node-level metrics. The profile's metric sets / built-in defaults still apply.

mib.note: A curated OID catalog. Pick metrics by name in the collection editor instead of typing OIDs.
mib.unavailable: The MIB catalog is unavailable in skeleton mode.

modal.vendorHint: Leave blank for a standard (non-vendor) OID.

delete.confirm: Delete catalog entry {{name}}? Collections referencing it by name will no longer resolve from the catalog. This cannot be undone.

discovery.note: Sweep a subnet for live + SNMP devices, then import the ones you want.

scans.title: Recent sweeps
scans.note: Sweeps this core is holding. Pick one to see its progress or its results.
scans.resumed: Showing a sweep that was already running.
scans.unknownScan: This core does not know that sweep — it restarted, or the sweep aged out. A poller may still be running it.
scans.pollFailed: Stopped checking this sweep after repeated errors. Reload to try again.
scans.queuedNote: Waiting for a poller to pick this sweep up. Nothing has been probed yet.
scans.stopRequested: Stop requested. The poller finishes what it is already probing, so this takes a few seconds.
scans.stopUnsupported: Stop requested, but a poller that could be running this sweep is too old to act on it — the sweep may run to completion.
scans.stoppedNote: Sweep stopped. The devices found before it stopped are below and can be imported.
scans.finishedAnyway: The sweep finished before the stop reached the poller.

pool.label: Sweep from
pool.anyHint: With no site chosen the sweep goes to whichever poller answers first — which may be one that cannot reach these addresses.
pool.deadHint: No live poller serves this site, so the sweep will go to whichever poller answers first instead.
pool.oneOf: One live poller in this site will run it.

seen.title: Seen on the network
seen.note: Addresses your monitored routers have actually spoken to that Yagra is not monitoring. Nothing here needs a scan — it comes from the ARP and IPv6 neighbor caches of the devices you already have.

coverage.off: No device has reported an ARP cache yet. Turn on the ARP / IPv6 neighbor cache walk under Settings ▸ System settings ▸ Discovery walks — until then this list is empty because nobody has looked, not because there is nothing to find.
coverage.complete: {{nodes}} device(s) reporting, {{observed}} address(es) resolved in total.
coverage.sampled: {{nodes}} device(s) reporting, {{observed}} address(es) resolved — but {{truncated}} of them hit the row budget, so this list is a sample of what is out there, not all of it.

err.import: failed to start monitoring that endpoint

icmpGate.label: Also try SNMP where ping is blocked
icmpGate.hint: Off: an address that does not answer ping is skipped instead of being tried with every credential, which is what keeps a large range quick. Turn it on to find devices that block ICMP but answer SNMP.

discovery.signIn: Sign in as an admin to run discovery.
discovery.credsLink: Discovery uses your stored credentials. <lnk>Manage credentials →</lnk>

msg.imported_one: Imported {{count}} node — they will start polling shortly.
msg.imported_other: Imported {{count}} nodes — they will start polling shortly.

err.badTargets: Enter IPs, CIDRs (≤/22), or ranges (e.g. 192.168.1.10-20), comma-separated — ≤1024 hosts total.
err.selectOne: Select at least one device to import.
